sources.entry: Dnote - A simple command line notebook with multi-device sync and web interface.

summary.one_liner: Dnote is a simple command-line notebook that stores notes in a single SQLite file, with optional sync between devices through a self-hosted server.
summary.what_it_does: Dnote lets you add, view, and search notes from the terminal, organized into books. Notes are kept in one SQLite file that you control. The README shows adding a note with a one-line command (or opening your editor if you omit the text), viewing a book's notes, and running full-text search. Optional sync moves notes between devices through a server you host yourself, and the server exposes a REST API. The server is distributed as a binary with SQLite embedded, and the README also shows running it with Docker Compose on port 3001 with a mounted data volume.
use_cases: Jotting down shell commands and snippets
Keeping notes in a portable SQLite file
how_to_run: curl -s | sh  (installer from the README; URL not included in the README text)
Download the binary from the releases page
dnote add linux -c "Check disk usage with df -h"
docker-compose up -d  (for the optional server, using a compose.yml that maps port 3001)
notable: Single binary with no runtime dependencies
All notes stored in one portable SQLite file
Self-hosted sync server with SQLite embedded, so no database setup is needed
Available through Homebrew and a Docker image
caveats: Sync requires running your own server; it is optional
The README does not describe a web interface, even though the listing mentions one
Installation script URL is missing from the README text provided
